wkclimb.assets.offer.ok: Your White Knuckle pack is up to date. It can be built again from your copy of the game, found here:
wkclimb.settings.title: White Knuckle Climbing
wkclimb.sounds.title: White Knuckle Climbing: sounds
wkclimb.settings.sound_volume.tooltip: Volume of all of this mod's sounds; the sliders below set each kind on top of it. 0% is White Knuckle's volume. Each kind still stops at the most it can get (see its slider). Default: 0%
wkclimb.settings.grabbing_volume.tooltip: Grabbing a handhold and letting go. 0% is White Knuckle's volume; up to +100% (twice as loud). Default: 0%
wkclimb.settings.landing_volume.tooltip: Jumping, climbing up onto a ledge, and landing. 0% is White Knuckle's volume; up to +100% (twice as loud). Default: 0%
wkclimb.settings.footsteps_volume.toolti: White Knuckle's footsteps (these replace Minecraft's while the pack is on). 0% is White Knuckle's volume; up to +100% (twice as loud). Default: 0%
wkclimb.settings.wind_volume.tooltip: The wind while you fall. 0% is White Knuckle's volume; up to +25%, where Minecraft's volume limit stops it on long falls. Default: 0%
wkclimb.settings.hurt_volume.tooltip: Getting hurt and dying. 0% is White Knuckle's volume; up to +100% (twice as loud). Default: 0%
wkclimb.settings.low_health_volume.toolt: The heartbeat and mortal-wound sounds at low health. 0% is White Knuckle's volume; up to +25%, where Minecraft's volume limit stops it near death. Default: 0%
wkclimb.settings.fatigue_volume.tooltip: The strain sound as your grip runs out, and slipping off when it's gone. 0% is White Knuckle's volume; up to +50%, where Minecraft's volume limit stops the slip-off sound. Default: 0%
wkclimb.settings.ice_volume.tooltip: Slipping and shaking on icy handholds. 0% is White Knuckle's volume. It can only go quieter: the game already plays it at full volume, Minecraft's limit. Default: 0%
wkclimb.settings.ledges_only.tooltip: Only the top edges of blocks can be grabbed, like White Knuckle. Off: any side of a block. Default: ON
wkclimb.settings.handholds_only.tooltip: Only blocks in the #wkclimb:handholds tag can be grabbed. Off: every solid block, like White Knuckle's "grab anything". Default: OFF
wkclimb.settings.reach_multiplier.toolti: How far your hands reach. 1.00x is White Knuckle's reach (2 blocks). Default: 1.00x
wkclimb.settings.exact_step_height.toolt: ON: White Knuckle's step height (0.18 blocks), so slabs and stairs must be jumped onto. OFF: Minecraft's. Default: OFF
wkclimb.settings.fov.tooltip: Field of view while climbing mode is on. 90 is White Knuckle's default; the lowest step uses Minecraft's own FOV setting. Default: 90
wkclimb.settings.hands.tooltip: Your first-person hands while climbing. White Knuckle: the game's own hands, from the pack built from your copy of the game. Minecraft: two arms in your skin, moving the same way. Click to switch.
wkclimb.settings.hands.tooltip.no_pack: White Knuckle's hands come from the pack, which isn't built yet, so you see Minecraft hands for now. Build it with Build... below. Click to switch.
wkclimb.assets.hands.title: Choose your hands
wkclimb.assets.hands.intro: How should your hands look while you climb? You can change this any time in the mod's settings.
wkclimb.assets.hands.wk.info: The game's own hands, built from your copy of White Knuckle.
wkclimb.assets.hands.credit: White Knuckle's hands © Dark Machine Games
wkclimb.assets.hands.minecraft.info: Two arms in your own skin that move like White Knuckle's.
wkclimb.assets.offer.minecraft_hands: You chose Minecraft hands. White Knuckle Climbing can still build White Knuckle's sounds, crosshair and blood from your own copy of the game, found here:
wkclimb.settings.enabled_on_start.toolti: Climbing mode is on when the game starts. Default: ON
wkclimb.settings.blocks_per_unit.tooltip: The world scale. It changes your eye height, reach and climbing speed together. 0.80 fits White Knuckle's player to Steve's height. Default: 0.80
wkclimb.settings.asset_prompt.tooltip: At the title screen, offer to build White Knuckle's hands and sounds when the pack is missing or out of date. Default: ON
wkclimb.settings.build.tooltip: Build or rebuild White Knuckle's hands, crosshair, blood and sounds from your copy of the game. Each step asks first.
wkclimb.hands.on: Climbing mode ON: hold left/right mouse to grab
wkclimb.hands.off: Climbing mode OFF: you can break and place blocks again
wkclimb.server_missing: This server doesn't have White Knuckle Climbing installed, so climbing is switched off here (otherwise the server would kick you for flying).
wkclimb.server_missing.short: Climbing is off: this server doesn't have the mod
wkclimb.assets.title: White Knuckle's hands and sounds
wkclimb.assets.offer.missing: White Knuckle Climbing can build White Knuckle's first-person hands, crosshair, blood and sounds from your own copy of the game, found here:
wkclimb.assets.offer.outdated: Your White Knuckle pack was made by an older version of this mod, and this version needs a newer one. It can be rebuilt from your copy of the game, found here:
wkclimb.assets.offer.steps: Nothing happens until you agree. Each step is explained first, with the exact folders it uses, and waits for your OK. You can stop at any step.
wkclimb.assets.offer.safety: The "Safety" section of the mod's README explains what this kind of access means for your computer.
wkclimb.assets.not_found: White Knuckle wasn't found in your Steam libraries. If you have it, choose its folder. (In Steam, right-click White Knuckle > Manage > Browse local files to see where it is.)
wkclimb.assets.not_found.flatpak: Your launcher runs as a Flatpak, a sandbox that can't see your Steam folder. If you have White Knuckle, choose its folder: that lets the launcher read just that one folder. It's usually in ~/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/common.
wkclimb.assets.not_found.config: You can also put its folder in config/wkclimb.properties as wk_game_dir, then restart Minecraft.
wkclimb.assets.not_found.config.windows: You can also put its folder in config/wkclimb.properties as wk_game_dir (for example wk_game_dir=D:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\White Knuckle), then restart Minecraft.
wkclimb.assets.picker.title: Choose the White Knuckle folder
wkclimb.assets.picker.info: Your system's own folder picker opens next. Choose the folder called White Knuckle (it has a folder called White Knuckle_Data inside).
wkclimb.assets.picker.info.saved: The mod saves where it is in config/wkclimb.properties (wk_game_dir) and only ever reads from it. It doesn't change anything else.
wkclimb.assets.picker.info.flatpak: Your system will then let your launcher, and everything running in it (every mod in every instance), read that one folder, from now on. Nothing else becomes visible to it. The next steps show how to take that access away again.
wkclimb.assets.leaves_fullscreen: Minecraft switches to a window while the other window is open, and back to fullscreen after.
wkclimb.assets.picker.open: Waiting for you to choose a folder in the folder picker...
wkclimb.assets.picker.wrong.hint: Choose the folder called White Knuckle: the one with White Knuckle_Data inside.
wkclimb.assets.flatpak.command: You can give the same access with a command instead. Press Copy command, quit Minecraft and close the launcher completely, paste the command into a terminal and run it (it prints nothing), then open the launcher again:
wkclimb.assets.flatpak.command.risk: It lets your launcher, and every mod in it, read White Knuckle's folder (only that folder) until you undo it with:
wkclimb.assets.flatpak.other_library: If White Knuckle is in a different Steam library (another drive or an SD card), or Steam itself is a Flatpak, change the folder in the command to where it really is.
wkclimb.assets.python.info: This opens a window that runs winget, Windows' own app installer, to install Python 3.13 from python.org (about 30 MB). It agrees to Python's license for you, and Windows may ask for your permission.
wkclimb.assets.python.info.after: When that window says "Press any key to continue", press a key, then press Try again here. No restart needed.
wkclimb.assets.python.info.remove: To remove Python later: Settings > Apps > Installed apps > Python 3.13 > Uninstall.
wkclimb.assets.checking: Looking for White Knuckle and Python...
wkclimb.assets.confirm.create_venv: This makes a folder for the asset tool's own copy of Python's libraries (about 20 MB to start with):
wkclimb.assets.confirm.install_libraries: This downloads UnityPy, TypeTreeGeneratorAPI, Pillow, numpy and soundfile, plus the small libraries they need, from pypi.org (Python's official package site) with pip. The exact versions are fixed by the mod.
About %s MB to download and about %s MB on disk, all inside:
It can take a few minutes. These are programs that run on your computer with your permissions: the README's Safety section explains what that means.
wkclimb.assets.confirm.build_pack.read: This reads White Knuckle's files here (it only reads them; it never changes them):
wkclimb.assets.confirm.build_pack.write: and writes the hands, crosshair, blood and sounds to:
wkclimb.assets.confirm.build_pack.size: About 3 MB, replacing what's there now. It takes about 15 seconds. Nothing is uploaded or shared.
wkclimb.assets.confirm.build_pack.portal: Your launcher can read White Knuckle's folder because you chose it. To take that access away later, run this in a terminal:
wkclimb.assets.confirm.enable_pack: This adds White Knuckle Assets to your active resource packs (saved in options.txt) and reloads Minecraft's resources, which takes a few seconds.
wkclimb.assets.confirm.enable_pack.reloa: The pack is already on. This reloads Minecraft's resources so the rebuilt pack is used, which takes a few seconds.
wkclimb.assets.undo.enable_pack: To undo: Options > Resource Packs, move it back to the left.
wkclimb.assets.running.install_libraries: Downloading and installing (this can take a few minutes)...
wkclimb.assets.no_python.windows: This needs Python 3.10 to 3.14, and it isn't installed. "Install Python 3.13..." explains what installing it does before anything happens. Or get Python 3.13 from python.org yourself.
wkclimb.assets.no_python.windows.install: When the install window has finished (it says "Press any key to continue"), press a key there, then press Try again here. If it showed an error, get Python 3.13 from python.org instead.
wkclimb.assets.no_python.linux: This needs Python 3.10 to 3.14. Install it with your package manager, then press Try again:
wkclimb.assets.no_venv: Python can't make its private library folder (its "venv" module is missing). On Ubuntu, Debian or Mint, run this in a terminal, then press Try again:

wkclimb.assets.not_found.configured: White Knuckle isn't in the folder set as wk_game_dir in config/wkclimb.properties:
wkclimb.assets.not_found.configured.fix: If you have it, choose its folder (that replaces the setting). Or delete the wk_game_dir line to look in the Steam libraries again.
wkclimb.assets.confirm.create_venv.nothi: Nothing else on your computer changes.
wkclimb.assets.failed.report.ask: Please report the problem at github.com/Fizz12215/White-Knuckle-Climbing/issues and attach that file.
